currentCard.prompt: Как называется лёд, который формируется непосредственно при замерзании поверхности океана?

answers.note: Морской лёд обычно отражает больше солнечной энергии, чем открытая вода океана.
Айсберг — отколовшаяся от ледника или шельфа крупная масса льда, плавающая в море.
Ледник — масса льда на суше, медленно движущаяся под собственным весом.
Шельфовый ледник обычно представляет собой плавучее продолжение материкового ледника у берега.

currentCard.explanation: Это морской лёд. В отличие от айсбергов, он возникает из солёной морской воды.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: QuickFacts L70 directly names frozen ocean water sea ice. The prompt asks the immediate direct-freezing material type, so key0 is unique: iceberg is a detached mass, glacier land-flowing accumulated ice, shelf a coastal floating structure. Sea-ice-derived coastal shelves are a later structural category and do not rename the immediate direct-freezing product. Distinct options remain plausible ice terms; this does not resolve the separate explanation material-origin overstatement.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Это морской лёд. В отличие от айсбергов, он возникает из солёной морской воды.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: First sentence correctly identifies sea ice. The second unqualified wording contrasts what the ice material originates from, rather than explicitly contrasting immediate formation mechanisms. QuickFacts L70 gives a simplified generic contrast, but detailed Larsen L123 admits sea-ice-only shelves and ShelfScience L75/L87 says shelves calve icebergs. Reader inference: that full context cannot support a universal exclusion of seawater-origin material from icebergs. Rephrase as direct freezing versus calving, retaining valid MAIN/key; this is not a salt-retention defect.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Айсберг — отколовшаяся от ледника или шельфа крупная масса льда, плавающая в море.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: ShelfScience L75-L78 defines detached chunks from shelves/glacier tongues that drift at sea as icebergs. The note correctly uses morphological calving origin, without excluding sea-ice-derived shelf material. It is consistent with the detailed shelf exception, unlike an unqualified material-source contrast.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Ледник — масса льда на суше, медленно движущаяся под собственным весом.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: GlacierScience L71/L77/L101 directly describes accumulated glacier ice flowing under gravity/its weight over land. The general slow-flow descriptor is not a numerical speed bound and does not deny L106 surges or sea-reaching termini. It teaches own glacier character rather than ocean freezing.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Шельфовый ледник обычно представляет собой плавучее продолжение материкового ледника у берега.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: ShelfScience L68-L73 describes the usual floating extension of continental glacier/ice-sheet ice at coast. The literal usually correctly respects Larsen L123 sea-ice-only exceptions; it no longer says every shelf must originate on land. Coastal morphology differs from the prompt’s directly frozen material name.

defects.literal: В отличие от айсбергов, он возникает из солёной морской воды.
defects.whyDefect: As written this is a categorical source-material contrast. Detailed retained primary explicitly allows entirely sea-ice shelves, and says all shelves calve icebergs. SOURCE acknowledges the exception for note3 but leaves the explanation’s broader contrast unqualified. The safe distinction is direct freezing versus detachment, not a universal exclusion of frozen-seawater material in every iceberg.
